title: Atomic Theory and Structure - Chemistry - Early Theories
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following statements from John Dalton’s original atomic theory was later proven incorrect by the discovery of isotopes?
options: Matter is composed of extremely small particles called atoms.
Atoms of different elements combine in simple whole-number ratios to form chemical compounds.
All atoms of a given element are identical in mass and properties.
In chemical reactions, atoms are combined, separated, or rearranged.
questions.explain: Dalton postulated that all atoms of a particular element are identical in mass. The existence of isotopes—atoms of the same element with different masses (different numbers of neutrons)—proved this specific postulate wrong.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In Rutherford's gold foil experiment, most alpha particles passed directly through the foil with no deflection. What did this observation suggest about the structure of the atom?
options: The atom is a solid sphere of uniform density.
The atom consists mostly of empty space.
Electrons are embedded in a positive jelly-like substance.
The nucleus occupies the majority of the atom's volume.
questions.explain: Since the vast majority of alpha particles passed through undeflected, Rutherford concluded that the atom is composed mostly of empty space, with the mass concentrated in a tiny nucleus.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which scientist proposed the "plum pudding" model, suggesting that the atom was a positively charged sphere with negatively charged electrons embedded within it?
questions.explain: J.J. Thomson proposed the plum pudding model after discovering the electron, conceptualizing the atom as a positive mass with electrons embedded like plums in a pudding.

questions.q: A chemist analyzes two compounds composed of carbon and oxygen. Compound A contains 1.33 g of oxygen per gram of carbon. Compound B contains 2.66 g of oxygen per gram of carbon. This observation best illustrates which law?
questions.explain: The Law of Multiple Proportions states that when two elements form more than one compound, the ratios of the masses of the second element that combine with a fixed mass of the first element can be reduced to small whole numbers (in this case, 2.66:1.33 is a 2:1 ratio).
